Are the lesions pustular or vesicular, and is there any evidence of conjunctivitis or respiratory distress?

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the Gram stain is normal, I need to rule out other infectious causes. Has the newborn had any fevers, poor feeding, or lethargy? Are the rash lesions sterile pustules on an erythematous base, and have you observed any discharge from the eyes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The clinical presentation of sterile pustules on an erythematous base sparing the palms and soles in a well-appearing 4-day-old is classic for transient neonatal pustular melanosis or erythema toxicum neonatorum. Given the normal Gram stain and lack of systemic symptoms, this is a benign self-limiting condition.
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema toxicum neonatorum
